title: A LONG WAR AND A HARDENED HEART

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Joshua waged war against all these kings for a long time. Except for the Hivites living in Gibeon, not one city made a treaty of peace with the Israelites, who took them all in battle. For it was the Lord himself who hardened their hearts to wage war against Israel, so that he might destroy them totally, exterminating them without mercy, as the Lord had commanded Moses - Josh 11:18-20 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Two things stand out here. First, the war took a long time. We often imagine faith as instant victory, but Israel's conquest stretched over years of hard fighting. If your own battles feel long and wearying, you are in good company. Faithfulness is usually a long obedience, not a single dramatic moment.

Second, and more mysterious, the text says the Lord hardened the hearts of these kings. This is a hard truth that Scripture does not shy away from, and neither will we. It does not mean God forced innocent people to sin. These were nations already set against God, already given over to great evil; in His justice, God confirmed them in the direction they had already chosen, as He did with Pharaoh (Rom 9:17-18). God's judgment sometimes takes the form of handing people over to the path they insist on walking (Rom 1:24).

Faithful Christians who love the Bible have long held this truth alongside human responsibility without pretending to fully untie the knot, and that is a good and humble place to stand. What we can say for certain is that God is never unjust (Gen 18:25), and He takes no pleasure in the death of the wicked (Ezek 33:11). Mercy was still on offer — the Gibeonites found it. Judgment is real, but so is the open door of mercy, and in Christ that door is thrown wide to all who will come (John 6:37).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Are you weary from a battle that has lasted longer than you expected?
- How do you hold God's sovereignty and human responsibility together humbly?
- Does it comfort you that the door of mercy in Christ stands open to all who come?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, some battles are long, and some truths are beyond me. Help me trust that You are always just and always merciful, and to run to the open door of grace in Christ. Amen.

cross_references.label: Cross References
cross_references.text:
(Rom 9:17-18; Rom 1:24; Gen 18:25; John 6:37)

Note: The hardening of hearts here has been understood by faithful believers in different ways; Scripture holds God's sovereignty and human responsibility together without fully resolving the tension. This devotional stays within that shared ground rather than pressing one theological system.
